transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-01-28 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 57m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood Solutions), Carlos (BluePeak CTO), Maya (BluePeak ML Eng), Ayesha (BluePeak Infra), Tom (BluePeak Product)

Summary section (auto-generated): Quick walk-through of model catalog, how we pick open model candidates, bench methodology, and compatibility matrix. Customer to share traffic profile for a pilot.

[00:00:05] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, this is Jordan from Redwood Inference. Um, quick round of intros?
[00:00:12] Carlos: Carlos here, CTO at BluePeak, we'll be evaluating models for our summarization and rerank pipelines.
[00:00:19] Maya: Maya, ML engineer, I'll run the bench with you and provide sample prompts.
[00:00:23] Ayesha: Ayesha, infra, I'm here for the VPC and deployment questions.
[00:00:28] Jordan: Great, thanks. Priya, do you want to kick off the catalog walkthrough?
[00:00:33] Priya: Sure, yeah. So first we'll open the catalog — so you can filter by task, size, license, and then there's our compatibility matrix on the right. Quick note: some names in the UI may show abbreviated vendor tags, sometimes transcriber calls it "Redwood dedicate" cause of audio, but it's Redwood Dedicated.
[00:00:55] [00:01:02] Priya: Here I've selected summarization and rerank, then we narrow to open models with permissive license. On this table we show performance profiles — median latency, tokens/s, and a quality indicator based on our eval sets.
[00:01:20] Maya: Are those eval sets public or do you use our prompts?
[00:01:24] Priya: We have a public baseline and you can upload private evals. For this pilot we recommend you upload a curated prompt set so the bench reflects production.
[00:01:40] [00:01:44] Liam: Also important — the bench harness supports both online latency runs and throughput sweeps for continuous batching; we capture P95, P99, CPU/GPU utilization and cost per 1k tokens.
[00:01:58] Carlos: Cost per 1k tokens for open models varies a lot. How do you normalize for quantized variants?
[00:02:05] Priya: Good question. We map quantization variants to compatibility tags. So a 4-bit quantized runtime will be listed as q4-compat and we'll show expected token cost plus a quality delta compared to fp16 baseline. There's some heuristics — if your task is short-turn chat we usually prefer a slightly larger fp16 that has lower latency for small seqs, but for long completions q4 often wins on cost.
[00:02:32] [00:02:38] Maya: In terms of kernel/hardware mapping, how reliable are the recommendations?
[00:02:42] Priya: It's based on our kernel selection matrix — we profiled models across Ampere and Blackwell-like hardware (we call them gen1, gen2 internally) and we estimate mem footprint and KV cache impact. But it's a heuristic not a guarantee. We always recommend running a quick bench run on your target instance to confirm.
[00:03:05] Ayesha: If we go private deployment in a VPC, are these bench runs doable in our environment or do you run them in Redwood test infra?
[00:03:12] Priya: We can run bench in your VPC if you give us ephemeral access keys, or you can run the bench harness yourself — we provide a dockerized runner and a runbook. For compliance reasons some customers prefer self-run.
[00:03:30] [00:03:35] Carlos: We have a 50 ms P95 requirement for the summarization endpoint under 200 req/s. Is that realistic?
[00:03:41] Jordan: Depends on model size and hardware. For 7B class quantized models on gen2 GPUs, hitting 50 ms P95 at 200 rps is tight — you'd likely need a dedicated pool and aggressive batching, maybe edge caching for prefixes.
[00:03:58] Maya: Could you show an example bench that demonstrates that tradeoff?
[00:04:03] Priya: Yeah, I have a saved bench here. Let me pull up the throughput sweep for model x7-open-rl — note the transcriber might show variants like "x7-open-rl" or sometimes the feed says x7-open-r l, minor errors in auto text.
[00:04:24] [00:04:30] Priya: This run shows online latency with continuous batching off and then with batching tuned. You can see P50 moves slightly but P95 drops significantly when we enable prefix KV cache because for summarization we re-use contexts a lot.
[00:04:47] Carlos: How do you measure cache hit rate?
[00:04:50] Priya: We instrument requests to compute prefix similarity and then log cache hits by key. The console shows hit rate and estimated token savings.
[00:05:02] Tom: For our product the important metric is tail latency during bursts — we need to avoid the 500 ms spikes.
[00:05:07] Liam: For spikes we recommend canary pools and automatic routing to a low-concurrency dedicated lane; Redwood's smart routing can divert to a less loaded region or model variant automatically. But that does add cost.
[00:05:25] [00:05:30] Ayesha: On the security side, we need SOC2 logs, KMS integration, and SSO — does Redwood Private include those?
[00:05:36] Jordan: Yes, Private offers KMS/HSM support, SAML/SSO integrations, and we surface audit logs with retention options. We'll share the security whitepaper after the call.
[00:05:48] Maya: One of our concerns is model drift — if we pick a model today and it degrades, what's the rollback story?
[00:05:53] Priya: The console supports rollouts with automatic regression detection against your eval set. If quality drops beyond a threshold we can auto-fallback to a pinned model variant.
[00:06:06] [00:06:12] Carlos: Could you run a quick demo of how you'd pick the shortlist? Like step-by-step?
[00:06:16] Priya: Sure. Step 1: task filter (summarization), step 2: license filter (open/commercial), step 3: quality baseline sort (our eval score on public benchmarks), step 4: apply hardware compatibility filter for gen2 and q4 variants, step 5: pick top N and run bench.
[00:06:35] [00:06:41] Priya: For BluePeak I marked three candidates: opensea-7b-ish (note: name may be transcribed wrong), x7-open, and a trimmed 13B q4 variant. I then queued bench runs for latency and throughput.
[00:06:55] Maya: How long do bench runs take? We want to iterate fast, ideally same-day results.
[00:06:59] Priya: Small latency runs can finish in 20-40 minutes. Full throughput sweeps and quality evals might take a few hours depending on your dataset size. We parallelize across pools to speed things up.
[00:07:14] [00:07:20] Carlos: When you show quality delta, what's the baseline — is it human eval or automated metrics?
[00:07:25] Priya: It's a mix: automated metrics for quick iteration (ROUGE/BLEU/embedding-sim), plus optional human evals for final checks. We show a delta against a selected baseline model — usually an fp16 reference.
[00:07:38] Tom: OK, in our case we'd likely need embedding similarity plus a custom rerank metric. Can you plug in our rerank scorer?
[00:07:43] Priya: Yes, you can upload a scorer function or provide a script; our bench harness will call it per candidate and return a ranked metric table.
[00:07:54] [00:07:58] Ayesha: On network egress costs — if we deploy private in our VPC, do we still pay Redwood egress fees?
[00:08:03] Jordan: For Private on-prem or VPC, egress is within your cloud account — there won't be Redwood egress billing. For hosted API there's standard egress as part of usage billing. We'll clarify in the pricing doc.
[00:08:17] Maya: Can we tag data residency regions for bench runs? We need EU-only for some customers.
[00:08:21] Priya: Yes, you can pin bench runs to region and specify dataset residency; the console respects that and uses regional pools.
[00:08:33] [00:08:40] Carlos: About fallbacks — if a quantized variant fails quality checks, will the router automatically go to fp16?
[00:08:44] Liam: You can configure a fallback policy: either to a specific model variant, to a different pool, or to a cheaper degraded mode. The policy can be threshold-based on quality, latency, or error rate.
[00:08:58] Maya: Can we see the JSON manifest for a model candidate? We want to audit layers and tokenizer versions.
[00:09:03] Priya: Yes, each model card includes a manifest with tokenizer, tokenizer_version, model files, and known caveats. Note there can be minor naming inconsistencies in the transcript; the UI shows the canonical slug.
[00:09:18] [00:09:25] Carlos: Let's talk about pilot size: what's a reasonable dedicated pool for our throughput target?
[00:09:30] Jordan: For 200 rps with 50 ms P95 target for small seqs, I'd estimate needing ~8 gen2 GPUs in a reserved pool with KV caching and per-request concurrency tuned. That's ballpark; bench will refine.
[00:09:47] Ayesha: Will that be billed hourly or committed?
[00:09:49] Jordan: Dedicated can be reserved monthly or committed for discounts. We can propose a 3-month pilot rate.
[00:09:58] [00:10:05] Tom: Any known gotchas when moving from hosted bench to private infra?
[00:10:10] Priya: Differences can come from kernel availability and NIC configs — sometimes kernels we use in our test fleet are slightly different than on-prem GPUs which affects perf. We capture kernel compatibility in the matrix and mark untested combos as "experimental."
[00:10:26] Maya: Could you show the compatibility matrix view?
[00:10:29] Priya: Yep here. Rows are models, columns are hardware types and quantization variants. Cells include recommended kernel and a color-coded fit: green ok, yellow experimental, red not recommended.
[00:10:44] [00:10:51] Priya: For example, this 13B q4-model shows green on gen2 with our q4 kernel, but yellow on gen1 due to memory pressure and KV cache thrash.
[00:11:03] Carlos: Are there automated suggestions for which models to test first?
[00:11:07] Priya: We have a scout score that weights quality, cost, and hardware fit against your constraints; you can tune weights. For BluePeak we nudged cost lower and quality still within target, so the scout recommended the trimmed 13B q4 and x7-open.
[00:11:27] [00:11:33] Maya: Any example prompts you'd recommend for summarization?
[00:11:36] Priya: Use a mix: short and long docs, noisy text, and edge cases. We'll share a curated set. Also include your rerank pairs so we can measure downstream impact.
[00:11:50] Jordan: Quick note — we'll attach the bench runbook and a sample prompt set after the call.
[00:11:56] [00:12:03] Carlos: What's the expected turnaround for a first bench pass if we hand you the prompts now?
[00:12:07] Priya: If we have access to S3 bucket and region pinned, we can kick off a small pass within the day and deliver results in 24 hours for latency runs.
[00:12:18] Maya: Can the harness simulate real traffic with bursts?
[00:12:22] Liam: Yes, we have a traffic emulator that can replay your captured traces or generate synthetic bursts with specified patterns.
[00:12:32] [00:12:38] Ayesha: On logging, do you keep raw request content in logs for hosted? We need PII controls.
[00:12:44] Jordan: For hosted, customers can opt-out of logging request bodies; Private gives full control. We also support redaction rules and token-level annotations.
[00:12:55] Carlos: Sounds good. Let's talk timeline — we'd like a pilot before end of Q1.
[00:13:00] Jordan: That's doable. Next concrete items: we'll share the runbook and pricing, you share prompts and traffic profile.
[00:13:09] [00:13:15] Tom: One last question — do you support multilayer rerank chaining? Like embeddings then ner then ranker?
[00:13:21] Priya: Yes, you can define pipelines in the console: embedding stage, vector DB, ranker callouts. Each stage's performance is captured and you can run end-to-end bench.
[00:13:33] Maya: Great. I'm curious about regression alerts — can they be tied to specific prompt buckets?
[00:13:38] Priya: Absolutely. You can tag prompt sets and set per-bucket thresholds; alerts will indicate the failing bucket so you can triage.
[00:13:48] [00:13:55] Jordan: Okay, thinking about next steps — Priya will send the bench runbook and the curated prompts, Carlos will share traffic profiles. We'll aim to reconvene for poc scoping next week.
[00:14:08] Carlos: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[00:14:12] Maya: Thanks, talk soon.
